data_sponsor.name: Data sponsor
data_sponsor.line: Executive who funds the governance programme and answers for it to the board.

governance_council.name: Governance council
governance_council.line: Group that sets shared policies and settles conflicts between areas.

data_owner.name: Data owner
data_owner.line: Business leader accountable for an area's data and for who uses it.

data_steward.name: Data steward
data_steward.line: Specialist who looks after definitions, rules and incidents day to day.

data_custodian.name: Custodian
data_custodian.line: Technical team that runs the platform and applies permissions exactly as the policy says.

data_consumer.name: Data consumer
data_consumer.line: Analyst or application that uses published data to decide.

field_technician.name: Field technician
field_technician.line: Uses operational data to plan and do work; needs no money or personal data.

auditor.name: Data auditor
auditor.line: Independently checks that controls work, without changing anything.

raci_letters.A: Accountable: approves and answers for it; exactly one per activity.
raci_letters.C: Consulted: gives an opinion before the decision.

layer_hint.bronze: Exact copy of what arrived from the source system. Never corrected: it is the evidence.
layer_hint.silver: Standardised and checked data. Anything that breaks a rule is held in quarantine.
layer_hint.gold: Data products ready for dashboards and reports, each with its contract.
layer_hint.file: File delivered by the source system.
layer_hint.exposure: Dashboard, report or analysis that consumes the data.

classification_hint.public: May be published outside the company.
classification_hint.internal: For internal use; no personal data or sensitive figures.
classification_hint.confidential: Sensitive business figures (prices, costs, margins) or contact data.
classification_hint.restricted: Employees' personal data, pay or identity documents.

completeness.name: Completeness
completeness.explain: Is everything that should be there present? For example, no order arrives without equipment.

uniqueness.name: Uniqueness
uniqueness.explain: Does each thing appear only once? For example, no two orders share a number.

validity.name: Validity
validity.explain: Do values make sense? For example, nobody works more than 24 hours a day.

consistency.name: Consistency
consistency.explain: Do records agree with each other? For example, hours are booked against orders that exist.

accuracy.name: Accuracy
accuracy.explain: Does the value match the source of truth? For example, the issued cost versus the material master.

timeliness.name: Timeliness
timeliness.explain: Did the data arrive on time? For example, new orders arrive within 3 days.

maturity_next.data_quality: Quality score history per table, with targets, alerts and an incident flow with deadlines.

value.legal: In Peru, personal data is protected by Law No. 29733. No fines are estimated here: only the internal effort of handling an incident.
value.how_text: Rows held per month = quarantined rows ÷ months observed. Rework = rows per month × hours per bad record. Decisions = rows per month ÷ bad records per decision × cost per decision. Arguments = indicators × hours × people. Personal-data risk = columns × hours per incident × yearly probability ÷ 12.

acerca.title: What is real and what is simulated in this demo
real_items: The engine that builds the tables, checks the rules and computes everything you see.
The rules, contracts, roles, access and glossary: versioned files checked on every change.
The results: every number in this app comes from the engine; if it does not match, the automatic check fails.
The tests and the log of checks, with links to every run.
simulated_items: The company “Servicios Andinos de Campo S.A.C.” and all its people, sites and customers.
The data: generated with a fixed seed and with defects planted on purpose.
The action buttons (release or discard rows) and the profile switch: there is no sign-in.
The value assumptions in soles: illustrative.
acerca.plan: How to take it to a real company: a 30-60-90 plan

plan_items.d: Pick one domain and its 10 most used indicators; name an owner and a data steward; write the glossary and first contracts; wire the automatic check.
Quality rules on the tables behind those indicators, quarantine and owner alerts; classification and role-based access; first monthly quality report.
Move grants, tags and masks to the platform; track the quality trend against targets; add the second domain and present maturity to the council.

jargon.RACI: Matrix that says, for each activity, who does it (R), who approves and answers for it (A), who is consulted (C) and who is informed (I).
jargon.ODCS: Open Data Contract Standard: an open format for writing data contracts.
jargon.DAMA: International data management association. Its guide, the DMBOK, organises data work into 11 areas.
jargon.DMBOK: DAMA's Data Management Body of Knowledge, which organises data work into 11 areas.
jargon.CI: Continuous integration: an automatic check that runs on every change and blocks what breaks a rule.
jargon.YAML: Simple text format for configuration files that can be versioned.
jargon.SLA: Service level agreement: for example, how often the data must arrive.
jargon.GRANT: Instruction that gives read permission on a table or column.
jargon.PR: Change proposal in the repository, reviewed before it is merged.
Closely held corporation, a company form in Peru. Fictional here.

contract_text.service_order_economics: For each non-cancelled order: planned versus actual cost, variance and gross margin.
contract_text.site_monthly_kpis: Orders, hours, cost, revenue and margin by site and month.
contract_text.inventory_position: Stock value, recent consumption, days of cover and replenishment alerts per material.
